title: The Mormon Pioneers' Trek to the Salt Lake Valley
traveller: Brigham Young and the Mormon pioneers
intro: Members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints left Nauvoo, Illinois, in 1846, after the death of their leader Joseph Smith made it clear the group could not remain there. In 1847 a vanguard company led by Brigham Young broke the trail west from Winter Quarters to the Great Basin.
ending: The first company reached the Salt Lake Valley in July 1847, then part of Mexico, where the Shoshone, Utes and Goshutes held sovereignty. By December 1847 more than two thousand Mormons had completed the journey, and migration continued in organised companies until 1869.

stops.text: The exodus from Nauvoo began on this day, after the killing of Joseph Smith in 1844 made it clear the Latter-day Saints could not stay. Advance parties were sent out by church leaders in March 1846.
stops.quote: On February 4, 1846 (the same day the Mormon exodus from Nauvoo began)

stops.text: Leaders planned the migration here during the winter of 1846–1847. On 5 April 1847 a vanguard of 143 men, three women and two children set out west with 73 wagons.
stops.quote: On April 5, 1847, at 2 p.m., the wagon train moved west from Winter Quarters toward the Great Basin.

legs.title: Across the plains and the Rockies

stops.text: The first segment took six weeks. The company halted to repair wagons and reshoe the animals, and was joined by sick members of the Mormon Battalion and by church members from Mississippi.
stops.quote: The first segment of the journey, from Winter Quarters to Fort Laramie, took six weeks, with the company arriving at the fort on June 1.

stops.text: The company took the established Oregon Trail and pushed through South Pass. Brigham Young had met the mountain man Jim Bridger on 28 June and discussed routes into the Salt Lake Valley.
stops.quote: The company pushed on through South Pass, rafted across the Green River and arrived at Fort Bridger on July 7.

stops.text: Another thirteen sick members of the Mormon Battalion joined the company here. Young chose to follow the trail the Donner–Reed party had used the year before, and he fell ill with mountain fever.
stops.quote: The company pushed on through South Pass, rafted across the Green River and arrived at Fort Bridger on July 7.

stops.text: The scouts Erastus Snow and Orson Pratt entered the valley, and the first camp was set up the next day. On 24 July Young, ill in a wagon, is reported to have said "This is the right place, drive on."
stops.quote: In July 1847, the first company reached the Salt Lake Valley, with scouts Erastus Snow and Orson Pratt entering the valley on July 21.

stops.text: Young and other chosen members of the vanguard company went back east to gather and organise the companies due in the following years.
stops.quote: In August 1847, Young and other selected members of the vanguard company returned to Winter Quarters.

notes: Iowa and the Great Plains are named only in passing; the article names no Iowa stop with an event, so none is given. Green River: the article puts Sam Brannan's meeting 'near Green River, Wyoming' in the last week of June and the rafting after South Pass, an order that does not fit the map; left out. The Platte crossing and ferry (Thomas Grover) have no named place; left out. South Pass has no date in the article. Fort Laramie's year 1847 comes from the surrounding narrative (article gives 'June 1' only). Nauvoo date is the exodus start per the Brooklyn section; the intro says advance parties went in March 1846. The article gives the Nauvoo temple's burning as 1848 and says 1846 tensions peaked; no extra stop. Native nations: the article names the Shoshone, Utes and Goshutes as holding sovereignty over the valley; the trail's Plains peoples are not named.
